newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: No date yet for Sri Lanka-Iraq tea-for-oil talks.
newsitem.headline: No date yet for Sri Lanka-Iraq tea-for-oil talks.

text.p: No date has yet been set for talks between Sri Lanka and Iraq on a possible tea-for-oil deal, a senior government official said on Monday.
"There was a proposal to send a delegation to Baghdad. But they have not fixed a date," the official, who declined to be identified, told Reuters.

The official was commenting on reports that a high-level delegation, led by Trade Minister Kingsley Wickremaratne and including a representative of the Ceylon Petroleum Corp, would leave Colombo soon for Baghdad to negotiate a deal.
The chairman of the Sri Lanka Tea Board, Clifford Ratwatte, said last week the talks would be held in the next few weeks.
But the government official said on Monday it was still not clear when the delegation would go to Baghdad.
Colombo's Sunday Times newspaper on July 27 quoted Ratwatte as saying the trip had been delayed but expressing confidence the trade mission would take place. It gave no further details.
Tea Board officials were not immediately available for comment.

Ratwatte said last week the deal was likely to be similar to a tea-for-oil deal India recently negotiated with Iraq and would come under an arrangement supervised by the United Nations allowing limited oil sales in return for food.

Iraq was barred by the United Nations from selling its oil after the 1991 Gulf War but is now allowed to sell up to two billion dollars worth of oil over 180 days to buy humanitarian goods, including food.
The senior government official said it was premature to speculate on the details of any possible deal resulting from the Sri Lanka-Iraq discussions, which he described as exploratory.
"It all depends on price," he said. "Our tea is relatively expensive."
He said Iraq was currently buying Sri Lankan tea but it was going indirectly, via other Mideast countries.
He declined to give figures or financial details.
Tea is Sri Lanka's biggest export earner, and is expected to bring in some 35 billion rupees this year, up from 32 billion in 1996, Sri Lanka Tea Board officials say.
